bladder_steps.title: Learn it hands-on first
bladder_steps.body: Watch us or your vet do it, then do it yourself with us guiding your hands. Written steps help you remember, but they are not a replacement for practice.

bladder_steps.title: Get calm and comfortable
bladder_steps.body: Hold {name} over the litter box, a sink or a puppy pad, supported against your body so they feel safe and do not slide.

bladder_steps.title: Find the bladder
bladder_steps.body: It sits in the lower belly, just in front of the back legs. When full it feels like a small water balloon.

bladder_steps.title: Cradle and press gently
bladder_steps.body: Cup the bladder between your fingers and thumb and press softly and steadily, back toward the tail, not up toward the ribs. Use the least pressure that makes urine flow.

bladder_steps.title: Keep going until it stops
bladder_steps.body: Hold the gentle pressure until the stream stops and the bladder feels small and soft. A bladder left half full can lead to infection.

bladder_steps.title: Clean and dry
bladder_steps.body: Wipe the belly and back legs with unscented wipes and dry well. Clean skin prevents urine scald and sores.

warning: the bladder feels very hard and nothing comes out with gentle pressure, there is blood in the urine, it smells very strong, there has been no poop in 2 days, or {name} cries, stops eating or seems unwell.

health.title: Pressure sores
health.body: Change position often and keep soft bedding. Check hips, knees and tail area for redness.

health.title: Urine scald
health.body: Urine left on skin burns it. Clean and dry after every expressing and keep the fur short.

health.title: Bladder infections
health.body: Paralyzed pets get them more easily. Regular urine tests at the vet catch them early.

health.title: Constipation
health.body: A high-fiber diet helps. Tell your vet after 2 days without pooping.

health.title: Muscles and joints
health.body: Gentle stretches and play keep legs supple. Ask your vet about physiotherapy.

health.title: A happy mind
health.body: Toys, cuddles and company. Special-needs pets live full, joyful lives.
